newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU may block purchase of Toys R Us Dutch units.
newsitem.headline: EU may block purchase of Toys R Us Dutch units.

text.p: Top European competition regulators have proposed blocking a Dutch retailer's purchase of Toys "R" Us operations in the Netherlands, European Union sources said Monday.

"There is a draft decision to forbid the alliance," but with a proposed way out for Blokker. Under the proposal, Blooker would take control of a smaller part of the Dutch operations of the world's largest toy retailer.

Blokker and Toys "R" Us, whose Dutch operations have never been profitable, have told European regulators there was no alternative to the proposed deal other than closing down the nine stores Toys "R" Us owns in Holland, sources close to the investigation said.
Blokker Holding BV agreed almost a year ago to buy the Dutch operations of Toys "R" Us after the retailer's losses piled up in the small but lucrative Dutch market.

Financial terms of the proposed deal remain undisclosed, but the agreement calls for Blokker to operate six of the nine Toys "R" Us stores. The companies have told regulators that the three other stores would be closed.

In a rare step, the Dutch government asked the EU's executive European Commission in January to investigate the transaction. The country has yet to implement rules on probing mergers and acquisitions.
Blokker controls about 60 percent of the Dutch toy market through its Bart Smit and Intertoys stores and household goods outlets, industry sources said. Toys "R" Us holds about 4 percent.
One source said other buyers have apparently been identified now. The commission has until July 3 to make a final decision.
Its draft decision, prepared by a merger task force, will be submitted to an advisory committee of competition experts Tuesday, another source said.
